newsitem.title: USA: Confessed murderer executed in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Confessed murderer executed in Texas.

text.p: A Houston man who confessed to shooting a Rice University student twice in the head and leaving her in a field to die was executed by lethal injection Wednesday.

John Kennedy Barefield, 32, admitted shooting architecture student Cindy Rounsaville after he and two accomplices kidnapped her at gunpoint from her apartment parking lot, robbed and then raped her in April 1986.

"I love y'all. Tell mama I love her," Barefield said to five of his relatives standing behind a glass wall to witness the execution while he lay strapped to a gurney at the Texas state prison in Huntsville.
He was injected with a dose of lethal chemicals shortly after 7 p.m. EST, gasped once and died seven minutes later.

Prosecutors said Barefield and two accomplices, his brother Perry Barefield and friend Lee Sonnier, were driving through the apartment parking lot looking for someone to rob when they spotted Rounsaville.

After forcing her into her car, they drove her to an automatic teller machine where she withdrew $70, all the money she had in the bank. The men then drove her to a remote area and sexually assaulted her in the back seat of her car.

While her abducters were arguing over whether to kill her, Rounsaville leaped from the car and ran across a field but was cut down by a bullet to the head. Barefield then stood over her still-moving body, put the gun near her head and shot her again, prosecutors said.
The only daughter of a Florida couple, Rounsaville, 25, was three weeks from graduation and engaged to marry her hometown boyfriend that summer, prosecutors said.

Arrested a month after the shooting on a separate charge, Barefield confessed to the murder after police found the victim's college ring in his possession. His .22 calibre pistol also was identified as the murder weapon, prosecutors said.
Barefield was implicated in four other armed robberies and told investigators he sought out white victims to rob while driving through apartment parking lots.
His brother, Perry Barefield, was sentenced to 45 years in prison and Sonnier was sentenced to life in prison for their roles in the abduction, rape and murder.

Barefield ordered a last meal of a double cheeseburger and french fries after spending his final day on death row visiting with his mother, three sisters, another brother and a niece. All of the relatives except his mother witnessed the execution.
None of Rounsaville's relatives witnessed the execution, which was the second of the year in Texas and the 109th in the state since capital punishment resumed in 1982.
Vigils were held outside the death house and in front of the Harris County district attorneys office in Houston to protest the death penalty.
